summary: Paul Horsch worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Paris and studied at Fribourg, Cambridge, Lausanne, and Marburg. He taught at Visva-Bharati (1952–1956) and held posts at the University of Zurich (1959, 1967–1971).

Paul J. Griffiths studied Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, completing degrees at Oxford and Wisconsin. He held posts at Chicago, Notre Dame, and the University of Illinois Chicago, later serving as Warren Professor of Catholic Thought at Duke (~2007–2017).
Paul K. Nietupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He received his PhD from Columbia University and was on the faculty at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Paul Kingsbury earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He worked in biomedical informatics at Mayo Clinic (2016–2019) and as a program manager at USC (2020–2022) and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (2022).
Paul Kiparsky is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Morris Halle at MIT (~1962–1965). He took up a post at Stanford University in ~1984.

Paul Kretschmer was a linguist who earned his PhD from Humboldt University of Berlin under Johannes Schmidt and Hermann Diels. He held posts at Berlin, the University of Marburg (1897–1899), and the University of Vienna as professor of linguistics (1899–1936).

Paul L. Swanson works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He served as a professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).
Paul Marriot Wynch was active in the field of Indology. He joined the Bengal Civil Service in 1808 and studied at the East India Company College from 1809 to 1810.

Paul Masson-Oursel worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Alfred Foucher, among others. He spent his career at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, serving as directeur d’études from 1927 to 1953.

Paul McBain specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Chicago and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (2018–2021), and became a lecturer at Thammasat University in 2021.

Paul Mendes-Flohr was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He served as director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and held a professorship at the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Michael Toomey was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Bowdoin College and completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1975–1984). He held posts at the American Institute of Indian Studies and Cornell University.

Paul Mus specialized in Buddhist and religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at EPHE, INALCO, and Paris. His career included posts at EFEO (1927–1940), EPHE (1937), Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale University (1950).

Paul Olaf Bodding was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at the University of Oslo (1883–1889). A member of The Asiatic Society from 1893, he served as head of The Santal Mission of the Northern Churches (1910–1933).

Paul Oltramare was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Geneva, Paris, and Basel. He taught at Collège Calvin (1876–1895) and the University of Geneva, serving as Docent of Sanskrit (1880–1881) and Professor of History of Religions (1893–1927).
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure in the early 1880s. He held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ~1894 to 1917.

Paul Pelliot was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Sciences Po, INALCO, and EPHE, and held professorships at the EFEO (1900) and the Collège de France (1909; 1911–1945).

Paul R. Brass was an Indologist who completed his education at Harvard College, the University of Chicago, and Harvard University (~1958–1964). He spent his career at the University of Washington (~1967–2001).

Paul Regnaud was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the EPHE and the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Lyon, serving as occupant of the Sanskrit chair from 1887 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur was a philosopher who studied at the University of Rennes and the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Strasbourg (1948–1956), Paris Nanterre (1964–1970), UC Louvain (~1969–1978), and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).
